summary:
TERRA-ANALOG is an advanced, web-based Geospatial Information System designed to bridge the gap between extraterrestrial exploration and terrestrial training. To address the challenge of identifying Earth analogs for permanent Moon and Mars bases, we developed a dynamic spatial matching engine powered by PostgreSQL and PostGIS. Instead of relying on static lists, our platform cross-references NASA's topographical, mineralogical, and environmental datasets  with Earth parameters .

The algorithm actively ranks terrestrial locations, like the Atacama Desert or Salda Lake, based on slope gradients and elevation contours, presenting them in an immersive, aerospace-grade dual-map interface. TERRA-ANALOG empowers mission planners to seamlessly generate automated field suitability dossiers, accelerating astronaut training and hardware testing for future interplanetary missions.
details:
How it works & Benefits:

TERRA-ANALOG operates by transforming raw space data into actionable intelligence. The backend ingests NASA NetCDF/TIFF files (such as MRO MOLA and LRO LOLA), processes the DEM (Digital Elevation Model) to extract slope gradients and elevation contours using Python (GeoPandas and Rasterio), and stores these parameters as spatial geometries in a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database. When a user selects a planetary target (e.g., Shackleton Crater), the PostGIS engine runs a spatial query to find Earth regions (using ASTER GDEM data) with intersecting environmental and topographical profiles, outputting a weighted similarity score.

Intended Impact:

The primary impact is accelerating mission readiness. By replacing manual geographical guesswork with a deterministic algorithm, space agencies can rapidly identify training grounds for rovers and astronauts, ensuring hardware is tested in the most accurate terrestrial extremes possible. Furthermore, it opens the door for localized geological research, allowing universities to identify regional analogs in their own countries.

Tools, Coding Languages, and Software:

  • Frontend: React, HTML5 Canvas (for disintegrating data visualization physics), Mapbox GL JS (for spatial rendering), Recharts (for elevation profiles).
  • Backend & DB: PostgreSQL with the PostGIS extension for spatial queries. Node.js/Python FastAPI.
  • Data Processing: Python (GeoPandas, NumPy).
  • Design: Custom industrial aerospace UI.

Creativity & Factors Considered:

We consciously avoided generic dashboard designs. Instead, we built an interface inspired by JPL Mission Control, utilizing strict aerospace aesthetics to maximize readability and immersion. We also considered scalability: the PostGIS architecture allows future integrations of crowdsourced analog reports (e.g., local citizens submitting geological photos of matched areas), bridging top-down satellite data with bottom-up human observation.
